_readme: Source of truth for the three grades. tools/build-grade-pages.py renders
grade-fine.html, grade-medium.html and grade-coarse.html from this file and
templates/grade.html. js/site.js also loads it at runtime for the depth
calculator's per-grade bulk density and the grain-scale illustration.
Grain size, mesh, bulk density and primary use come from the brief and are
the values to build against. Everything marked TODO is invented placeholder
data and must be replaced before launch; see README.md.

grades.name: Fine
grades.title: Fine aragonite sand for reef tanks, 0.5–1.0 mm | AragoCor Aragonite
grades.description: Fine grade Bahamian aragonite sand, 0.5–1.0 mm (18–35 mesh), for reef and sand-bed aquariums. Screened, lot-tested, bagged in Stockton, CA in 20 lb retail and 50 lb trade bags.
grades.tagline: The reef grade. Fine enough to settle into a flat, even bed and to suit sand-sifting gobies and wrasses. Screened to keep the fines that cloud a new tank out of the bag.
grades.card_use: Reef and sand-bed tanks. Settles flat, holds a clean line against the glass, and suits burrowing gobies and wrasses. Needs gentle flow at the substrate.
grades.other_blurb: The reef grade. Settles flat and suits sand-sifting livestock. Needs gentle flow at the substrate.
grades.sieve_note: A tight distribution is what keeps a fine bed level. The bottom row is the one that causes cloudy water, so we publish it.
grades.calc_intro: Shallow reef beds run half an inch to an inch. Deep sand beds run three to four. Measure the footprint, not the tank volume.
grades.calc_note: Round up. A fine bed compacts over the first few weeks and settles lower than it goes in.

uses.title: Reef and sand-bed tanks
uses.body: Settles into a flat, even bed with a clean line at the glass. The look most reef keepers are after, and the grade that shallow sand beds are built on.

uses.title: Sand-sifting livestock
uses.body: Suits gobies, sleeper gobies, sand-sifting starfish and wrasses that bury at night. Coarser grades are hard on gill rakers and on burrowing behaviour.

uses.title: Not for high flow
uses.body: Fine sand lifts and drifts under strong bottom flow, and it will pile against the rockwork. If your powerheads sweep the substrate, take the medium grade instead.

grades.keywords: fine aragonite sand reef tank, aragonite sand bed, sugar-fine aragonite alternative, oolitic aragonite sand

grades.name: Medium
grades.title: Medium aragonite sand for marine and mixed reef tanks, 1.0–2.0 mm | AragoCor Aragonite
grades.description: Medium grade Bahamian aragonite sand, 1.0–2.0 mm (10–18 mesh), for general marine and mixed reef aquariums. Holds under stronger flow. Screened, lot-tested, bagged in 20 lb retail and 50 lb trade bags.
grades.tagline: The forgiving grade. Stays put under stronger flow than fine sand and still reads as a natural flat. If you are not sure which grade to run, start here.
grades.card_use: General marine and mixed reef. The forgiving grade. Stays put under stronger flow, still fine enough to look like a natural flat. Start here if you are not sure.
grades.other_blurb: The forgiving grade. Holds against stronger flow and still reads as a natural flat. Start here if you are unsure.
grades.sieve_note: Most of the bag sits in the middle two bands. That is what keeps a medium bed from sorting itself into a fine layer on top and a coarse layer underneath.
grades.calc_intro: One to two inches is the usual range for a medium bed. Measure the footprint of the tank, not its volume.
grades.calc_note: Round up if you want the bed to stay level after it settles. Sand compacts over the first few weeks.

uses.title: Mixed reef and fish-only marine
uses.body: Holds its place under the flow a mixed reef runs, and still looks like a flat rather than gravel. The default for a tank that has to please both fish and corals.

uses.title: Tanks with strong return flow
uses.body: Where a fine bed would drift and bare the glass, medium stays down. Detritus still settles on top where a clean-up crew can reach it rather than sinking into the bed.

uses.title: Not for sand sifters
uses.body: Sleeper gobies, sand-sifting starfish and burrowing wrasses want a grain they can pass through their gills and mouths. If the tank is built around them, take the fine grade.

grades.keywords: medium aragonite sand, aragonite substrate marine tank, aragonite sand mixed reef, 1-2 mm aragonite

grades.name: Coarse
grades.title: Coarse aragonite substrate for cichlid and hard-water tanks, 2.0–5.0 mm | AragoCor Aragonite
grades.description: Coarse grade Bahamian aragonite, 2.0–5.0 mm (4–10 mesh), for African cichlid tanks, hard-water freshwater, high-flow marine and filter media. Screened, lot-tested, bagged in 20 lb retail and 50 lb trade bags.
grades.tagline: The cichlid and hard-water grade. A larger particle that stays put under strong flow, supports alkalinity in a tank that is pulling it down, and works as a filter media where a bigger grain is wanted.
grades.card_use: African cichlid tanks, hard-water freshwater, and high-flow marine. Also used as filtration media where a larger particle is wanted.
grades.other_blurb: African cichlid and hard-water freshwater tanks, high-flow marine, and filter media where a larger particle is wanted.
grades.sieve_note: Almost nothing below 2 mm. A coarse bed with fines in it clouds on setup and then packs. This one does neither.
grades.calc_intro: Cichlid tanks usually run two to three inches so the fish can dig. Measure the footprint of the tank, not its volume.
grades.calc_note: Coarse grain settles less than fine sand, but diggers will pile it. Round up if the tank has diggers.

uses.title: African cichlid and hard-water tanks
uses.body: Rift-lake cichlids and livebearers want hard, alkaline water, and a carbonate substrate helps hold it there between water changes. The grain is large enough for diggers to move and for the bed to stay open.

uses.title: High-flow marine and filter media
uses.body: Stays down under the flow that would strip a fine bed. In a sump or reactor the larger particle keeps water moving through the media rather than channelling around it.

uses.title: Not for a natural reef flat or for sifters
uses.body: Coarse reads as gravel, not sand, and detritus falls into it where a clean-up crew cannot reach. It is wrong for sand-sifting fish and for anyone after a smooth reef bed. Take fine or medium instead.

grades.keywords: aragonite substrate cichlid, coarse aragonite gravel, aragonite for hard water aquarium, aragonite filter media
